text:
maya: Pushed overnight embeddings run for tsunami-embed-v1. Quick headline: float32 beats prod (heron-v2) on our semantic holdouts (recall@1 +0.025), int8 per-channel quant retains most quality (recall@1 +0.013 vs prod). Silhouette avg up (0.12 -> 0.14). Full artifacts: s3://redwood-evals/tsunami/2026-03-21

alex: Nice. which holdouts did you use?

maya: 20k holdout: en/wiki+QA, short-queries (<=6 tokens), and multilingual subset (en/es/fr/de). Also contrastive samples from CC12M as an auxiliary check.

sam: Any weird failure modes?

maya: Short queries show the largest quant gap at k=1. Example pair where float sim 0.82 -> int8 0.49, affects top-1. Most pairs are within 0.02. I'll attach top 50 regressions.

liam: Can you paste the high-level numbers?

maya: Sure. summary table (recall@k):
```
Prod(heron-v2)  R@1 0.720  R@5 0.905
Tsunami float   R@1 0.745  R@5 0.912
Tsunami int8    R@1 0.737  R@5 0.909
```
Delta @1 (int8 vs prod) = +0.017. Delta @1 (int8 vs float) = -0.008.

alex: Good. Did you test cosine vs dot? quant can change norms.

maya: Yes — cosine yields slightly better stability under quant. Dot product had a ~0.012 extra drop at k=1 for int8 on short queries. We default to cosine in eval.

sam: Tokenizer mismatch possible? which tokenizer/version?

maya: tokenizer v3 (subword), same as prod. No stopword stripping.

liam: Can we try a per-channel int6 sweep? Might reduce model size while keeping quality.

maya: Kicked off an int6 per-channel sweep on a 10k holdout (batch 256). Queue id: ci-embed-1745. Will report results in this thread.

ops-bot: Deployment preview created for staging: /staging/tsunami-embed-v1/quant-int8 on dedicated pool (tag: q-int8-stg).

alex: I'll do a quick manual review of the top 30 regression pairs and flag any obvious data/annotation issues. Assigning to myself.

maya: thanks. also ran clustering sanity (UMAP + HDBSCAN) — cluster counts and sizes consistent with float; small clusters reshuffled but top-N centroids preserved. UMAP params: n_neighbors=15, min_dist=0.1, metric=cosine.

sam: good. can you run a recall@1 with L2 normalization post-quant? sometimes rescaling helps.

maya: adding a pass that normalizes vectors after quant decode and before cosine. Script: `python eval/compare_recall.py --model tsunami --quant int8 --norm post`

liam: propose a canary threshold: max acceptable delta at R@1 = -0.01 relative to float, and relative to prod we require >= prod R@1. If int8 fails, we fallback to float for dedicated customers.

alex: +1 for canary thresholds. Also add UMAP silhouette and a small human-review set (20 examples) for semantic drift.

maya: Plan: finish int6 sweep, run post-quant normalization, compare cosine/dot, produce 1-page decision note with example pairs and decide canary thresholds by EOD.

liam: thank you — ping when results in.

alex: :thumbsup:
